reading.body:
Elizabeth Frazee is named on 76 AI lobbying filings, all filed through a single firm, with the largest client share going to a software trade association.

The filings cluster around a small set of clients. SIIA accounts for 14, Science Applications International for 12, and LinkedIn, T-Mobile, X Corp, and the Internet Infrastructure Coalition for 10 each. The remaining clients, Tools for Humanity and Zebra Technologies, account for 6 and 4. One lobbyist, one firm, and a client list weighted toward trade associations, government contractors, and communications platforms is the pattern the data supports.

Every one of the 16 points that records a prior government position names the same offices: counsel or legislative director to Rep. Bob Goodlatte, communications director to Rep. Tom Bliley, and press secretary for the House Energy and Commerce Committee. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, so the repetition reflects the same disclosed history appearing across separate filings rather than sixteen distinct roles. Energy and Commerce is the committee with jurisdiction over communications and technology, which is the subject matter of the filings listed here.

What the data does not show is what any filing actually asked for. It records who was named, for which clients, and how often, and nothing about the positions taken, the bills targeted, or the outcomes. It also does not connect this lobbying to data center siting, power procurement, or any other physical constraint on compute. The link between AI policy work and the buildings and electricity that AI depends on is not in this data, and should not be read into it.

summary: Elizabeth Frazee is named as a lobbyist on 76 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 53268. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
